rv.q: But in Jinkx Monsoon, another star rises.
A production that is, in most respects, exceptional.

The Talk of the Town, one of the most glamorous nightclub venues in London at the time, offered Garland a lucrative contract and the possibility of a comeback before wealthy audiences and celebrity admirers.
It is an electrifying introduction, sharply silhouetted against the darkness of our knowledge, and from that moment onward, the audience is utterly locked onto Monsoon’s extraordinary performance.

The entire cast do a great job at helping build the world around Judy Garland’s stardom, with Adam Filipe (playing Judy’s pianist, Anthony) convincingly bringing a tenderness of heart one rarely encounters in people. The other company members’ generosity paves the yellow-brick road for Jinkx Monsoon’s soaring performance as Judy Garland.

cn.t: Jinkx Monsoon electrifies as Judy Garland in this exposing portrait of the icon's 1968 London comeback, blending vaudevillian charm with unflinching depictions of addiction and stardom's brutal cost.

dr.inst: Released via TodayTix app only at 10 AM.
